items.note: The three-letter thesis of the paper as a diagram: three 3-D cylinders in a row - Pressure (blue), State (green), Response (orange) - joined by four straight arrows each carrying its own label (Pressure P-to-S, Information S-to-R, Response R-to-S, Resource S-to-P) and closed into a triangle by two curved arcs labelled Impact (P-to-R) and Response (R-to-P). No legend, no axes, no numbers: the arrow labels ARE the key, and the cylinder fill colour only repeats the label inside each node. The cylinders are icon glyphs, not a third dimension. It floats in the right column beside the body of section 3.1, so its caption prints under the artwork and to the right of the heading - the heading detector read the two as one line, '3.1 PSR Figure 1: PSR Model'. Never cited: the prose immediately below it discusses P, S and R without ever pointing at the figure that names them.

The paper's whole indicator system delivered as a TABLE wearing a figure caption: seventeen rows (one header, sixteen indicators) and five columns - Target Layer, Dimension Layer, Theme Layer, Indicator Layer, and a fifth column of +/- marks with NO header at all, so sixteen marks are unexplained. Merges run on the row axis only: 'Fragility Index' spans all sixteen indicator rows, the three dimensions span six, five and five, and the seven themes span their own blocks. Rules are not booktabs - heavy closed top, header and bottom borders with DASHED separators at every dimension and theme boundary and dashed verticals between the layer columns - and the grouping is carried by pastel colour bands rather than by shading. The same sixteen indicators are then written out as a bulleted list in the two pages that follow, so the figure and the prose say the same thing twice. Introduced only as 'we determine the indicators shown in the figure below' - no number.
items.other_note: a ruled indicator-hierarchy table printed as the figure - 17 rows by 5 columns, pastel cell bands and dashed group separators, no axes, no plot

items.note: Directed node-link diagram of the climate chain the section argues for: a heavily thinned graph in three tiers of 3, 5 and 5 nodes - climate drivers (Temperature, Elevation, Natural Disasters) into land and water processes (Forest Cover Rate, Crop Production, Water Resource, Health, Energy Consumption) into social outcomes (GDP, Gini Coefficient, Public Service, Democracy Rate, Human Right). Edge colour encodes the SOURCE tier (blue leaves the top tier, orange the middle, green the bottom, one yellow edge leaves Temperature) and no legend explains it, so the colour carries information the reader must infer from the node fills. Several edges run upward from the social tier back into the land tier, drawing a dense X of crossings with no bundling and no arrowheads large enough to follow at page size. No edge weights, so the figure states the topology of the argument and none of its strengths - those arrive a page later as regressions in Table 2. Never cited by number: it appears under the sentence 'we are required to identify how climate change increases fragility directly and indirectly' and the two bulleted lists that follow are its caption in prose.

items.note: The validation exhibit: twenty numbered cases on a fragility axis, each case carrying TWO marks - a light-blue open circle for the model's PSA score and a red-orange cross for FSI's - with the case number hand-placed beside the pair. Two horizontal threshold rules cut the field at 0.6 (purple) and 0.4 (orange) and the band names are printed as red text in place of a legend, so the key lives half in the caption and half in the plot. No axis titles at all, only ticks (x 0-10, y 0.2-0.9), so the reader is told nothing about what either axis measures. The caption does the keying that a legend would: 'Blue circles represent the results of PSA, and red crosses rep-resent the results of FSI', with no space after the colon and the hyphen of a line break left in 'represent'.

Single-series time path of the DRC's fragility index, MATLAB default styling: light-green line with dark-green downward triangles at eleven annual points, title inside the frame ('Fragile Index over the past eleven years of DRC'), boxed axes with inward ticks and no grid. Axis titles present here - 'Fragile Index' and 'Year' - which the validation scatter of Figure 4 did not get. The y axis is cropped to 0.30-0.36, a sixth of a unit tall, so ordinary annual wiggle fills the frame; the sibling Figure 6 plots the same index on 0.28-0.44 and Figure 7 on 0.32-0.42, so no two charts of the same quantity share a scale. The prose introduces it as 'ten years data' and the chart titles eleven points. Never cited by number: the reading that follows is a narrative of the 2008-2010 cholera and the 2012 drought, not a pointer.

Legend inside, upper right, boxed, two keys, both ungrammatical ('with the climate change', 'without the climate change'). Title inside the frame. items.note: The sensitivity study the paper promised, and the only chart in it with more than two series: five open-triangle lines for the five settings of the AHP weight, 2006-2016, legend boxed inside at lower right. Both the legend and the caption have LOST the Greek letter - the keys print '01 = 0.8' and the caption 'Analysis of 1' where the weight symbol should be - so the parameter this whole section varies is unnameable from either. No axis titles on this one (the only chart after Figure 4 without them), y 0.0-0.5 on a 0.1 step, five curves inside a band about 0.05 wide: the flatness is real, and it is also what a 0.5-tall axis makes of any band.

note:
Coverage. All 27 physical pages were read at text level and all 23 measured regions were inspected on a crop. Table 1, the symbol table of p7, was confirmed from the PDF geometry instead of a crop, because it owns no region: two columns of Symbol and Description under a caption printed between the top rule and the header row, so the text layer's first header line reads 'Symbol  Table 1: Symbol table / Description'. The five excluded regions, in page order: the normalisation equations (1) and (3) on p10 as two pasted strips; equation (9) with the entropy step on p12; the piecewise classification rule that defines Equation 12 on p15, printed as a brace over three conditions; and the FSI half of Table 3 at the head of p16. 

The census arithmetic. Nineteen printed exhibits, eighteen of them measured. Nine are charts, numbered Figure 1 to Figure 9 and all of them uncaptioned as charts should be captioned; ten are grids, of which four are numbered Table 1 to Table 4, four are numbered nothing at all (two on p21, two in the appendices on p26), and two are numbered as FIGURES. The loss is one grid, Table 1, and the cause is the one #164 established: a booktabs grid whose only ink is three thin rules has no area to cluster, so the cleanest table style in the corpus is the one the detector cannot see. 

Two caption systems, one page. The body numbers its grids Table 1 to Table 4 with a colon. The appendix numbers its grids in a chapter style, 'Table 2.6' and 'Table 2', and those titles are pasted INSIDE the images, so they never reach the text layer. On top of them the text layer prints 'Figure 10: Climate Expenditure: 2011-2014' and 'Figure 11: Climate Expenditure: 2015-2017' under two grids that are unmistakably tables - three merged super-headers, rotated sub-columns, boxed frames, a source line. A reader who follows the figure numbers arrives at two tables; a reader who follows the table numbers arrives at four of the ten grids and at two numbers that collide with each other. This paper therefore cannot be read by number at all, which is why eleven of its eighteen measured exhibits are introduced only positionally. 

No three dimensions, and no two charts of one quantity on one scale. The paper is entirely two-dimensional and carries no colourbar, but it plots the fragility index on four different y windows - 0.30-0.36 for the DRC, 0.28-0.44 for the DRC counterfactual, 0.32-0.42 for Bangladesh and 0.35-0.65 for the forecast - so no two curves in the paper can be compared by eye, and the DRC curve whose whole point is a small recent upturn is the one drawn on the narrowest window. Figure 4 has no axis titles at all; Figure 9 has none either; the rest do. 

Tables. The numbering is the story: four numbered grids (one of them unmeasurable), four unnumbered, two misnumbered. Style follows no rule - three booktabs, five boxed with internal verticals, one with no rules at all - and the boxed ones are exactly the appendix and the three-number transposition, i.e. the tables that were probably imported from a spreadsheet rather than typeset. Precision is uncontrolled: the cost forecast runs one to four decimal places in one column, PSA prints three decimals beside FSI's four, and Table 2 prints its decimal points as colons. 

Apparatus. The red Chinese resale banner prints across six pages including four that carry exhibits. The folio runs five behind ('Page 22 of 22' on p27 of 27) and the contents page claims 22 pages against 27 printed. Equation numbers inside the classification rule and inside the pasted equations are images, so 'Equation 12' is cited in the prose on p15 and neither its number nor its body is in the text layer. The two p27 tables sit in Appendix B, which the contents page does not list at all.
rules: 27 physical pages, 23 measured regions on 16 of them, and eighteen of the regions are printed exhibits: nine charts (Figures 1-9) and nine grids [place.doc_order].

Table 1, the symbol table on p7, owns no region at all: it prints as three horizontal rules with no closed outline, so the clustering pass drops it - the same fault that cost #164 its Tables 3 and 4 [place.area_frac].
Five regions are not exhibits: four pasted display equations (p10 twice, p12, p15) and the FSI half of Table 3 carried over the 15/16 page break [place.doc_order].

Two caption systems run in parallel and they disagree about what the object is: the body numbers Figures 1-9 and Tables 1-4, while the p27 grids are captioned 'Figure 10' and 'Figure 11' from the text layer over their own pasted titles 'Table 2.6' and 'Table 2' [caption.numbering].
Nine charts split line 5, scatter 1, flowchart 1, node-link 1, table-as-figure 1 - a line chart is this paper's default exhibit for every quantity it computes [geometry.family].

Figure 2 is a table-as-figure: the sixteen-indicator hierarchy is a 17-by-5 ruled grid with pastel cell bands and dashed group separators, captioned as a figure and never referenced by number [geometry.family].
Nothing in the paper is three-dimensional, nothing carries a colourbar, and no two rows share an axis - the only multi-series charts are Figures 6 and 9 [geometry.three_d].

Legends run none 7, inside 2: seven of nine charts key nothing at all, two of them (Figures 6 and 9) key inside the frame, and Figure 4 replaces its legend with red band names printed on the plot [geometry.legend].
Every chart prints its numbers - ticks, and in Figure 4 the twenty case numbers laid beside their marks [geometry.printed_numbers].
Caption side is below on all nine figures, which is the one consistent thing about this caption layer [caption.position].
Table captions do not hold still: eight print below their grid and one above (Table 3) [caption.position].

No caption in the paper uses a verb - voice is none on all eighteen rows, every one a bare noun phrase from 'Figure 2: Indicators' to 'Figure 6: Comparison of Congo's FI with and without climate change's effect' [caption.voice].
Captions run 3 to 19 words; the longest, Figure 4's, is the only one that does work beyond naming, because it carries the key the chart has no legend for [caption.words].

Not one caption draws a conclusion and not one names a variable or a unit - the quantitative content of this paper lives in the axes, which are untitled on Figures 4 and 9 and cropped to a different window on every chart of the same index [caption.concludes].

Figure 4's caption is a legend in disguise: 'Fragility Index:Blue circles represent the results of PSA, and red crosses rep-resent the results of FSI', with no space after the colon and a line break left in the word [caption.verbatim].

Figure 9's caption has lost the symbol it is about - 'Analysis of 1' where the AHP weight should be - and its legend keys read '01 = 0.8', so the parameter the whole sensitivity section varies cannot be named from either [caption.verbatim].

Table styles split boxed 5, booktabs 3, no-rules 1: the numbered main-body tables are booktabs, the appendix grids and the transposed Table 4 are boxed with internal verticals, and one appendix grid has no rules at all [table.rule_style].

No grid in the paper is zebra-striped; the shading that exists is categorical - pastel field bands in the figure-table, orange on one appendix header block, uniform green over the other [table.zebra].

Three grids merge cells and they merge in three different directions: Table 3 merges its country list down the row axis, the p27 tables merge their header across columns, and Table 2 merges its indicator name down two fitted equations [table.merged_cells].

Exactly one grid puts a unit in its header ('CC relevant Allocation (amount in thousand taka)'), and one prints its unit outside the frame entirely ('(Crore taka/BDT 10 million)') [table.units_in_header].

No grid aligns its decimals, although four carry numbers: the cost forecast drifts from one decimal place to four in one column, and the appendix matrices print PSA to three places beside FSI to four [table.decimal_aligned].
Table 1 aside, the widest measured grid is the appendix comparison matrix at 482 pt against a 451 pt measure, so the one unruled table is also the one that runs into the margins [table.width].
The tallest grid is Appendix A's at 21 rows and 20 countries, and it carries no caption and no number - the appendix heading does the work a caption normally does [table.rows].
One grid is 13 columns wide, its three merged super-headers each spanning four sub-columns whose labels are set rotated vertically [table.cols].
One grid is continued across a page break (Table 3), and the continuation prints with no header repeat, no 'continued' mark and no repeated caption [table.continued].
Seven exhibits are pointed at by number; eleven of the eighteen carry no number in any pointer at all [mention.first_page].

Four exhibits are introduced positionally instead of by number - 'shown in the figure below', 'the table below', 'as shown in the following table' - so a reader keyed on 'Figure N' misses a third of the exhibition [mention.lead_pattern].
lead_pages is 0 on six of the seven cited rows and -1 once: Table 3 is cited on p16 while its grid begins on p15, the only exhibit the paper points BACKWARD at [mention.lead_pages].
Lead patterns split direct 5 and figure-n-shows 2, and 'as shown in' never appears [mention.lead_pattern].
Section kinds split result 6, model 4, appendix 4, test 2, symbols 1, sensitivity 1 - the two case studies alone carry five of the nine charts [place.section_kind].
Zones run top 9, middle 4, bottom 5, so half the exhibition opens its page [place.page_zone].
Areas run mean 13.6 per cent, maximum 27.8 (Figure 6, the counterfactual) and minimum 1.3 (Table 4, three numbers in a two-row grid) [place.area_frac].
No exhibit owns a page to itself; every one shares its page with prose or with a sibling exhibit, and p15, p21 and p27 each carry two [place.solo_page].
The four appendix tables are the only exhibits whose section is unnumbered - the appendix headings do the captioning for them [place.section_numbered].
Table 2's fitted values print with a COLON for a decimal point - 'Water = 1:099 t + 42:15' - the LaTeX colon-decimal fault, and one line has lost its '+' operator [table.note_sentence].
The red Chinese resale banner prints across the top of p15, p16, p18, p19, p21 and p23, and the folio runs five pages behind the physical page ('Page 22 of 22' prints on p27 of 27) [place.area_frac].

tables.note: One grid holding two competing classifications of the same twenty states: a PSA block (header 'PSA | Country Code' plus Fragile, Vulnerable, Stable) and directly under it an FSI block with its own header and its own three bands, separated by a single inner horizontal rule and framed top and bottom with no verticals anywhere. The country list is one MERGED multi-line cell per band, so the grid is really nine cells, not thirty. It breaks over the 15/16 fold: the PSA block and FSI Fragile print on p15, FSI Vulnerable and Stable on p16 with no header repeat, no 'continued' mark and no repeated caption - the p16 strip is the excluded region. The comparison the caption promises does not survive its own cells: PSA's three bands hold 20 distinct states, FSI's hold 19 because BR is printed twice in the Vulnerable list, so the two columns cannot be reconciled. Cited on the page AFTER the table starts, where 'From Table 3,Our model's classification' also carries a missing space after the comma.

The first of the paper's four uncaptioned grids and the one that breaks its own numbering: six intervention programmes mapped to the indicators they move, seven rows by two columns, printed with NO caption, NO table number and NO title - the prose introduces it only as 'as shown in the following table'. Much larger than the four numbered tables and far less finished: horizontal rules in booktabs style but with one stray VERTICAL rule between the two columns that starts below the top rule, and one cell (Intervention2) holding five stacked indicator names so that its row is four times the height of its neighbours. Predicted indicators and effects are mixed in one column with no unit, no ranking and no direction of change. Uncaptioned, so the caption block records an empty verbatim and numbering 'none'.

The cost forecast, and the second uncaptioned grid: seven rows (header plus six programmes, with a Total row riding under them) by five columns - program, Current, in 5 years, in 10 years, in 20years. Booktabs with the BOTTOM RULE MISSING, so the grid has no closing line and the Total row floats unclosed. Header typo 'in 20years'; decimal precision drifts inside a single column from one place to four (1735.9, 2474.39, 8530.6122) and the columns are not aligned on the point, so the numbers cannot be scanned down. No unit anywhere, although every cell is a fiscal expenditure - the prose says the figures come from Bangladesh budget documents in crore taka. Introduced as 'Total expenditure and budget allocations ... are as followed:'.

mention.lead_sentence: Frome Table 4, we can clearly see that Europe get the highest score and Africa get the lowest one.

tables.note: Three numbers as a table: four continents across the top and one row of fragility indexes, 0.8176, 0.3218, 0.2849 - a transposed grid in which what is normally the stub becomes the header, four columns and two rows. The only BOXED grid in the main body: closed outer frame plus internal verticals, no shading, about half the measure, four decimals throughout. Its caption prints BELOW, and the sentence that reads it misspells 'From' as 'Frome'. The lowest cell of the three is Africa at 0.2849, on the same 0-1 scale where a state is fragile below 0.4 - so the table says the whole continent is fragile and the prose says the model works.

Appendix A's result table: the twenty countries of section 3.4 with their PSA score and their FSI rank, four columns by twenty-one rows, carrying no caption and no table number at all - the appendix heading 'Appendix A FI of Country' does the work a caption would. Fully BOXED, outer frame and every internal horizontal and vertical rule, the heaviest grid style in a paper whose numbered tables are booktabs. No unit, no decimal alignment (scores are centred), three decimals in the FI column and bare integers in the rank column. It is the table Figure 4's twenty numbered scatter points refer to ('The corresponding contries are listed in the Appendix A'), printed thirteen pages after the chart that needs it, which is the paper's only cross-reference from artwork to data.
